reviews.classification: historical synthesis and qualified dependency/conflict map
reviews.disposition: C1–C23 are proposed resolutions grounded in their original authority, not 23 new accepted rules. Preserve optional capability-kind extension, texture/evidence versus tiny modifiers, schema-owner boundaries, demand tier versus disclosure, actual transmission timing, local capacity/clean/full/no-cost variants, distinct trained/acquired source, projected view versus multiple dashboards and borrowed source versus paid result. C12’s single-milestone condition is retired, and current B107 corrects blanket no card-specific heir carry while leaving general lineage/world retention unproved. C5’s local-root fallback is not the default merely because historical P1 merge was unknown; B111 inspects the existing stream service. C23’s generic render-before-save statement is qualified by B84/B110/B112, without claiming CV1 itself verified. C10 uses current desktop/text targets, not only the original 1366 floor. Preserve all original corrections without retroactively granting new code or broad source certification.
reviews.evidence: Complete current original body read including all graph edges, contract tables, conflict rows, timed refreshes and input prefixes. Underlying lane reports retain independent ledger coverage; no graph rendering or runtime proof.
reviews.reopen: Current selected consumer may revise a named edge or conflict from accepted direction and actual source; no whole body-engine campaign, wait schedule or new gate is selected.

G30 no longer needs a single-prestige milestone choice; a selected continuation/carrier operation still needs stable identity and actual retained-world/estate settlement. Source/graph/hash checks establish neither current APIs nor native delivery; AD51 permits shared-seam design from known needs before another implemented case.
